review.title: Previously treated extrahepatic disease
review.context: Use when colorectal cancer has involved any site outside the liver (after primary resection, removed together with the primary, or as local relapse), including disease later resected, ablated, irradiated or in response to treatment.
review.stance: Keep previously treated extrahepatic disease closed in the initial CRLM pathway. Propose one narrow study stratum for limited, completely treated lung-only metastases; every other site stays closed.
rules: Default: extrahepatic metastasis after primary resection (including nodes outside the primary resection field), extrahepatic metastasis removed with the primary, and local relapse are outside the initial pathway, even after resection, ablation, radiotherapy or complete response. Response to systemic therapy alone never counts as clearance.

Proposed lung-only study stratum (not active; needs its own protocol, institutional and IRB approval, and a living-donor or individually reviewed allocation route): pulmonary metastases only, at most three lesions in total, each completely treated with curative intent (R0 resection preferred; stereotactic radiotherapy or ablation only with documented local control), no thoracic nodal involvement on pathology or PET-CT, and no recurrence outside the liver for ≥12 months after the last lung treatment.

The stratum adds no other relaxation: every CRLM-B3 limit still applies (BRAF wild type, MSS/pMMR, R0 primary, CEA <80 ng/mL, no pretreatment liver lesion >10 cm, documented disease control), and chest CT and PET-CT within one month show no disease outside the liver. Do not combine it with another expansion.

Hilar nodes: frozen section of hilar nodes before implantation, and before donor hepatectomy in living donation; a positive node ends the transplant. In Oslo, 7 of 72 listed patients were stopped at laparotomy for hilar nodal metastasis.

Closed, with no proposed stratum: nodal disease outside the primary resection field; peritoneal, ovarian, adrenal, bone, brain or other non-lung sites; local relapse; more than three lung lesions; thoracic nodal involvement; or recurrence after lung treatment. A new or indeterminate extrahepatic lesion during evaluation or on the waiting list is HOLD for characterization and restaging; it does not enter the stratum.
review.tests: Dated history of every extrahepatic site: imaging, operative and pathology reports, radiotherapy or ablation records and margins; thoracic nodal status; number and size of lung lesions; interval from primary resection to lung disease and from the last lung treatment to evaluation; chest CT and PET-CT within one month; dated CEA series. Plan intraoperative hilar node frozen section before implantation (and before donor hepatectomy).
review.allocation: NLRB guidance excludes extrahepatic disease after primary tumor resection (including lymphadenopathy outside the primary lymph-node resection) and local relapse from an initial CRLM MELD exception, and requires no development of extrahepatic disease for extension. A standardized deceased-donor exception is therefore not available. The lung-only stratum would need living-donor transplantation within an approved study or an individual NLRB request that states the deviation; this proposal implies neither.

evidence.synthesis: Lung-limited colorectal metastasis is the most indolent extrahepatic pattern, and the transplant experience points the same way. On retrospective review of SECA-I chest CT, 7 of 21 recipients already had untreated pulmonary metastases at transplantation, and 6 of them were among the longest survivors; no statistical test was reported. Lung metastases after transplantation grew no faster than in non-transplanted controls (median doubling time 125 versus 130 days), and the 14 Oslo recipients whose lung recurrence was resected had 64.5% ten-year survival from lung resection. IHPBA advises that isolated pulmonary recurrence after transplantation be considered for resection. Newer protocols admit limited, treated lung disease: SECA-III excludes recent resection of non-hepatic metastases and any previous bone, CNS or thoracic or abdominal nodal metastasis, and a Japanese living-donor study accepts up to three treated lung metastases without recurrence for more than six months. This supports studying a lung-only stratum, not opening it.
evidence.counterevidence: Direct evidence is one patient. In SECA-II arm D, the recipient whose lung metastasis had been resected eight years earlier was recurrence-free at 23 months, but the arm overall did poorly (median DFS 4 months, OS 18 months) because several adverse features were combined. IHPBA states there is no evidence to support transplantation in patients who present with or subsequently develop extrahepatic metastases; TransMet excluded prior or current extrahepatic disease and local recurrence; and NLRB excludes post-resection extrahepatic disease. In PulMiCC, lung metastasectomy did not clearly improve survival (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.56–1.56), so successful lung treatment may select favourable biology rather than cure it. After liver resection, nodal and peritoneal extrahepatic disease had markedly shorter survival than lung disease (median 26 and 29 versus 45 months).
evidence.certainty: Very low for transplantation after previously treated extrahepatic disease (one reported recipient); low for the indirect inference that lung-limited disease behaves indolently after transplantation; no transplant evidence for previous nodal, peritoneal or other sites.
evidence.threshold_basis: At most three lung lesions follows the Japanese living-donor protocol. Twelve months without recurrence after lung treatment sits between that protocol (more than six months) and SECA-III, which excludes resection of non-hepatic metastases within the last two years and of pulmonary or liver-hilum lymph-node metastases within the last year. Excluding thoracic nodal involvement reflects its strong adverse effect after lung metastasectomy in patients with previously resected liver metastases (HR 4.86). None of these limits has been tested in transplant recipients.

studies.design_population: Multicentre randomized trial of liver transplantation plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone; 94 randomized.
studies.selection: Required no extrahepatic disease and excluded prior or current extrahepatic disease and local recurrence.
studies.results: Five-year overall survival 56.6% versus 12.6% by intention to treat (HR 0.37).
studies.limits: Provides no data on patients with previous extrahepatic disease; its benefit cannot be extrapolated to them.

studies.design_population: 2021 international Delphi consensus on transplantation for non-resectable colorectal liver metastases.
studies.selection: Statement 9: there is no evidence to support transplantation in patients who initially present with or subsequently develop extrahepatic or extracolonic metastases. Statements 10–12: high-resolution chest CT and FDG PET-CT to rule out extrahepatic disease; nodal sampling when suspicion is high and PET is inconclusive.
studies.results: Statement 41: isolated pulmonary recurrence after transplantation should be considered for resection. The text notes that many lung recurrences were retrospectively visible at transplantation and do not grow faster under immunosuppression.
studies.limits: Expert consensus. It treats extrahepatic disease as a sign of disseminated disease and does not separately address completely treated lung-only disease.
studies.locator: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2021;6:933–946; statements 9–12 and 41, recurrence discussion.

studies.design_population: Prospective SECA-II arm D expanded-criteria cohort; ten recipients.
studies.selection: Unlike SECA-I and SECA-II, patients with resectable pulmonary metastases or previous resection of pulmonary metastases were eligible. One recipient had a pulmonary metastasis resected eight years before transplantation (node-negative sigmoid primary, at most two liver metastases).
studies.results: Only two of ten were recurrence-free (23 and 26 months); one was the recipient with the previously resected lung metastasis. A second recipient had an ovarian metastasis removed with the primary 14 months before transplantation and relapsed in the lung at 5 months. Overall median DFS 4 months and OS 18 months; the lung was the first relapse site in six.
studies.limits: One relevant patient within a cohort that combined several adverse biological, anatomical and donor features; it cannot estimate the effect of prior lung disease.
studies.locator: BJS Open 2020;4:467–477; Methods, Table 2 (patient 1) and Discussion.

studies.design_population: Prospective SECA-I cohort, 21 recipients; recurrence-pattern analysis with re-review of pre-transplant chest CT.
studies.selection: Liver-only disease was required at inclusion.
studies.results: Thirteen of 16 single-site first recurrences were pulmonary; on retrospective review, 7 recipients already had untreated pulmonary metastases at transplantation and 6 were among the longest survivors.
studies.limits: Small cohort; the lesions were untreated and found retrospectively; no statistical test; not evidence that treated lung disease is safe.

studies.design_population: Case–control imaging study: 11 SECA recipients with 18 resected lung metastases versus 12 non-transplanted rectal cancer controls.
studies.selection: Lung metastases arising after transplantation.
studies.results: Median tumour-volume doubling time 125 versus 130 days by diameter; five-year overall survival after first pulmonary resection 51% in the transplant group.
studies.limits: Small selected groups; addresses growth after transplantation, not eligibility after previous lung disease.

studies.design_population: Oslo cohort: 14 of 55 recipients whose first relapse was pulmonary and treated by resection.
studies.selection: Pre-transplant liver PET metabolic tumour volume (MTV) used for stratification.
studies.results: Ten-year overall survival from lung resection 64.5%; 85.7% with MTV <70 cm³ versus 25.0% above. Eight had no evidence of disease 7–131 months after lung resection.
studies.limits: Post-transplant recurrence in a small selected group; does not test transplantation after treated lung disease.

studies.design_population: Oslo randomized trial of transplantation versus chemotherapy or other treatment after progression on, or intolerance of, first-line chemotherapy; target 30.
studies.selection: Allows resectable lung lesions, all <15 mm. Excludes previous resection of local relapse or non-hepatic metastasis within the last 2 years or resection of pulmonary or liver hilus lymph node metastases in the last year, and previously diagnosed bone, CNS or thoracic/abdominal nodal metastases.
studies.results: Recruiting; no results posted.
studies.limits: Registry wording for a different population (progression on first-line therapy); eligibility may change.

studies.design_population: Japanese multicentre single-arm living-donor transplantation protocol (11 university hospitals; target 23).
studies.selection: No distant metastasis except the liver, but patients with no more than three lung metastases and no recurrence for more than six months after treatment are eligible; RAS and BRAF mutations are not exclusions; central eligibility review. No size limit is set.
studies.results: Protocol only; outcomes not yet reported.
studies.limits: The authors describe the criteria as relatively broad; no control arm.
studies.locator: BMJ Open 2024; eligibility criteria and strengths/limitations.

studies.design_population: Randomized trial of pulmonary metastasectomy versus no metastasectomy; 93 randomized at 14 hospitals.
studies.selection: One to six resectable lung metastases at a median 2.7 years after colorectal resection; 29% had prior liver metastasectomy.
studies.results: Adjusted hazard ratio for death within five years 0.87 (0.51–1.48; unadjusted 0.93, 0.56–1.56); five-year survival 36.4% with metastasectomy versus 29.6% without.
studies.limits: Closed at 31% of the planned 300; inconclusive; not a transplant population.

studies.design_population: Pooled individual-patient analysis of 146 patients undergoing pulmonary metastasectomy after previous curative liver resection (five studies).
studies.selection: Lung metastases detected a median 23 months after liver resection.
studies.results: Five-year overall survival 54.4% and recurrence-free survival 29.3% from lung resection; thoracic lymph-node involvement was the only independent adverse factor (HR 4.86, 95% CI 1.56–15.14).
studies.limits: Retrospective selected surgical series; not transplant recipients.

studies.design_population: Systematic review of liver resection for CRLM with extrahepatic disease: 50 studies, 3481 patients.
studies.selection: Hepatic resection in the presence of extrahepatic disease; heterogeneous timing and treatment.
studies.results: Median survival by extrahepatic site: lung 45 months, portal or para-aortic nodes 26 months, peritoneum 29 months.
studies.limits: Non-transplant, heterogeneous observational studies.

studies.design_population: Official OPTN/NLRB guidance: Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology.
studies.selection: CRLM exclusions for an initial exception: extrahepatic disease after primary tumor resection (including lymphadenopathy outside the primary lymph-node resection) and local relapse. Extension requires no development of extrahepatic disease. Staging: CT/MRI of chest, abdomen and pelvis and PET within one month of the initial request.
studies.results: Allocation guidance; no outcome data.
studies.limits: Governs MELD-exception review, not clinical suitability or living-donor eligibility.

studies.design_population: Oslo pooled cohort; 72 listed, 61 transplanted.
studies.selection: PET-CT before transplantation; prior extrahepatic disease not analysed.
studies.results: 10 of 72 listed were not transplanted because of extrahepatic disease, 7 with hilar nodal metastasis on frozen section at laparotomy; intention-to-treat 5-year survival 42.6%.
studies.limits: No control group.

studies.design_population: North American living-donor series; 91 evaluated, 10 transplanted.
studies.selection: Liver-confined disease with sustained control; abdominal exploration before the donor operation.
studies.results: 1 of 10 had PET-negative portal nodal metastasis in the explant and recurred in the peritoneum at 121 days.
studies.limits: Ten patients.
studies.locator: JAMA Surg 2022; Table 4 and Results (full text).

edits.old: no macrovascular invasion, extrahepatic disease or unmeasurable infiltrative tumor.
edits.new: no macrovascular invasion, current or previous extrahepatic disease (HCC-B5) or unmeasurable infiltrative tumor.

edits.old: no extrahepatic disease, and ≥12 continuous months
edits.new: no current or previous extrahepatic disease (HCC-B5), and ≥12 continuous months

review.title: Previously treated extrahepatic disease
review.context: Use when HCC has involved any site outside the liver (regional or distant lymph nodes, lung, adrenal, bone or peritoneum), including disease later resected, ablated, irradiated or in complete response to systemic therapy.
review.stance: Keep closed. Previous extrahepatic metastasis is outside the standard pathway and every HCC high-risk cohort, even after local treatment or a complete response to immunotherapy. Record durable complete responders in a registry; this edition offers no transplant route.
rules: “No extrahepatic disease” in HCC-B1 and HCC-B2 means no current or previous extrahepatic metastasis. Resection, ablation, radiotherapy or a complete radiological response does not clear this history.

Count proven lymph-node metastasis, including hilar or hepatoduodenal nodes, as extrahepatic disease. Enlarged hilar nodes without proof (XXL treated a short axis >2 cm as extrahepatic spread) are HOLD for characterization. A lesion later proven benign is not prior extrahepatic disease; record how it was resolved.

Registry, not listing: enter patients with a durable complete response of extrahepatic disease, with dated imaging, AFP and treatment history. Starting points for any future study (not active): at least 12 months without evidence of disease off systemic therapy; PET or tissue confirmation that every extrahepatic site is cleared; current whole-body staging including bone; an immunotherapy washout of at least 90 days and the HCC-B3 safety review.
Do not combine with the expanded-burden (HCC-B1) or portal-vein invasion (HCC-B2) cohorts.
review.tests: Complete extrahepatic history (site, pathology, dates, treatment, response); chest CT and bone imaging; AFP series; immunotherapy agents, response and last dose; how any indeterminate extrahepatic finding was resolved.
review.allocation: NLRB guidance lists extrahepatic metastatic disease as a contraindication to an HCC exception score, and OPTN Policy 9.5 requires a chest CT to rule out metastatic disease and CT or MRI to rule out other extrahepatic spread. Neither addresses disease that has been cleared; any future request would be an individual narrative request with no assured outcome.

evidence.synthesis: Every HCC transplant framework reviewed requires absence of extrahepatic disease, and AASLD lists lymph-node involvement or extrahepatic spread as downstaging failure and an exclusion from transplantation. ILTS–ILCA recommends downstaging, and immunotherapy for downstaging, only in patients without extrahepatic disease, and the XXL trial excluded extrahepatic spread, including hepatic-hilum nodes with a short axis >2 cm. Lymph-node involvement was strongly adverse after transplantation (HR 2.60 for death in noncirrhotic livers; pooled odds ratio 10.44 for recurrence with positive hilar nodes). A complete response is not cure: among 160 complete responders to immunotherapy-based treatment, prior extrahepatic metastasis doubled the risk of recurrence (adjusted HR 2.00), and 5-year recurrence-free survival in the whole cohort was 18%. The only published transplant after metastatic HCC is one case: the best response of nodal, lung and bone disease to nivolumab was partial, the bone lesions did not clearly regress, liver disease recurred off treatment and was ablated, extrahepatic clearance was never confirmed by biopsy or PET, and the recipient was free of cancer one year after transplantation.
evidence.counterevidence: Durable complete responses to checkpoint inhibitors are now seen in advanced HCC, and the case shows transplantation is feasible after such a response. The guidelines describe current extrahepatic disease only; excluding previously treated disease is this program’s inference, not a guideline statement. ILTS–ILCA notes there is not yet enough evidence to say whether patients with a complete radiological response to immunotherapy still need transplantation or how long to observe them, so a permanent bar is a policy choice rather than a proven boundary. Immunosuppression could accelerate residual microscopic extrahepatic disease, which favours a registry with long observation over case-by-case transplantation.
evidence.certainty: Very low for transplantation after previously treated or completely responded extrahepatic HCC (one case report). Moderate that current nodal or extrahepatic disease predicts poor post-transplant outcome.
evidence.threshold_basis: The 12-month starting point mirrors the minimum 12 months of stability NLRB describes for selected candidates after ruptured HCC or primary portal-vein branch invasion, and the ILTS–ILCA 12-month observation after downstaging of Vp1–2 invasion; it is not derived from extrahepatic-disease data. The ≥90-day washout follows the AASLD advice to stop checkpoint inhibitors at least 3 months before transplantation and the rejection signal with washouts of 90 days or less in a multicentre cohort.

studies.design_population: 2024 ILTS–ILCA Delphi consensus with external review.
studies.selection: Downstaging is recommended for patients beyond local criteria without extrahepatic disease and without portal-vein macrovascular invasion; immunotherapy might be used for downstaging in patients without extrahepatic disease, within trials. For Vp1–2 invasion, a minimum 12-month observation after downstaging may allow assessment of tumour biology.
studies.results: No statement supports transplantation after extrahepatic disease. The text notes insufficient evidence on whether complete radiological responders to immunotherapy still need transplantation or how long to observe them.
studies.limits: Expert consensus; the immunotherapy statements carry weak grades.
studies.locator: Liver Transpl 2025 and Liver Cancer 2026 (PMC13271748); HCC working-group statements.

studies.design_population: Official OPTN/NLRB guidance: Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology.
studies.selection: Contraindications to an HCC exception score: macrovascular invasion of the main portal or hepatic vein, extrahepatic metastatic disease, ruptured HCC and T1 HCC. Some candidates stable for a minimum of 12 months may be considered despite rupture or primary portal-vein branch invasion.
studies.results: Allocation guidance; no outcome data.
studies.limits: Silent on previously cleared extrahepatic disease.

studies.design_population: Randomized trial of transplantation after successful downstaging of HCC beyond Milan criteria.
studies.selection: Main tumour-related exclusions: extrahepatic spread on CT or MRI, hepatic-hilum lymph nodes with short axis >2 cm, and portal-vein tumour thrombosis or invasion.
studies.results: Five-year overall survival 77.5% with transplantation versus 31.2% without, from randomization.
studies.limits: Excluded the population of interest; its benefit cannot be extrapolated to previous extrahepatic disease.
studies.locator: Lancet Oncol 2020; Methods (exclusion criteria) and protocol appendix.

studies.design_population: European Liver Transplant Registry: 105 recipients with unresectable HCC in noncirrhotic livers.
studies.selection: Transplantation as primary treatment (62) or for intrahepatic recurrence after resection (43).
studies.results: Lymph-node involvement (HR 2.60) and macrovascular invasion (HR 2.55) were independently associated with death; five-year survival 59% without either.
studies.limits: Noncirrhotic population; nodal status as recorded by centres, not previously treated nodal disease.

studies.design_population: Single case report.
studies.selection: Advanced HCC with abdominal and mediastinal nodes, lung and bone metastases in alcohol-related cirrhosis; nivolumab for about 17 months with a best response of partial response (RECIST 1.1); bone lesions did not clearly regress; liver disease recurred about 3 months after stopping nivolumab and was ablated; transplantation about 10 months later.
studies.results: Free of cancer one year after transplantation.
studies.limits: One patient with 1-year follow-up; extrahepatic clearance was not confirmed by biopsy or PET, and no nodes were examined in the explant; the authors caution that immunosuppression may facilitate progression of extrahepatic disease.
studies.locator: J Gastrointest Oncol 2025; case presentation (full text).

studies.design_population: AASLD 2023 practice guidance (relevant sections read).
studies.selection: Table 4 lists lymph-node involvement by tumor or extrahepatic spread as downstaging failure and exclusion from transplantation.
studies.results: Recommends stopping immune checkpoint inhibitors at least 3 months before transplantation.
studies.limits: No section addresses transplantation after treated extrahepatic disease.

studies.design_population: Four-centre cohort of 160 complete responders to immunotherapy-based treatment.
studies.selection: 58 (36%) had extrahepatic metastases when immunotherapy started.
studies.results: Prior extrahepatic metastasis: adjusted HR 2.00 (1.43–6.38) for recurrence after complete response; 5-year recurrence-free survival 18% in the whole cohort.
studies.limits: Retrospective; conversion subgroup not split by extrahepatic status; internal numeric inconsistencies.

studies.design_population: Eight-centre matched cohort, 416 recipients initially beyond Milan.
studies.selection: Extrahepatic metastasis was an exclusion (9 recipients left out).
studies.results: Immunotherapy-based downstaging associated with better survival (HR 0.63); acute rejection 16.3% vs 8.2%, clustered with washout of 90 days or less.
studies.limits: Not evidence for treated extrahepatic disease; transplanted-only cohort.
studies.locator: JAMA Oncol 2026; Figure 1 and Results (full text).

studies.design_population: Meta-analysis of transplant series: five on recurrence and five more on survival.
studies.selection: Hilar nodes examined at transplantation.
studies.results: Tumor-positive hilar nodes associated with recurrence (common odds ratio 10.44, 95% CI 3.43–38.59).
studies.limits: Small, older series; nodes mostly found at transplantation.

review.title: Previously treated nodal or extrahepatic disease
review.context: Use when iCCA has involved regional lymph nodes or any site outside the liver, including disease that later responded to chemotherapy or was resected or irradiated.
review.stance: Keep closed. Proven malignant nodes or extrahepatic disease, current or previously treated, exclude the small-cirrhotic route and the advanced-iCCA study. Confirm node-negative status pathologically before listing.
rules: Previously proven malignant regional nodes, even after radiological or pathological response, and any previous distant metastasis (peritoneum, lung, bone, distant nodes) are outside the initial iCCA routes. Resection of an extrahepatic site does not clear this history.
Suspicious or indeterminate nodes are HOLD until resolved pathologically; an imaging response is not nodal clearance.

Proposed for the advanced-iCCA study: before listing, sample any suspicious node (EUS-FNA or surgical) and sample the common hepatic artery (station 8) and hepatoduodenal ligament (station 12) nodes surgically; for living donation complete this before listing, not only at the combined donor–recipient laparotomy. A positive result ends the transplant route. Perform regional lymphadenectomy at transplantation.
Indeterminate extrahepatic lesions (subcentimetre lung nodules, bone lesions) need biopsy or interval imaging before listing; “stable on chemotherapy” is not clearance.
Previously node-positive disease that has cleared is a separate future research question; do not combine it with multifocal, G3 or living-donor expansions.
review.tests: Original and current nodal imaging with a station map; nodal pathology (EUS-FNA, operative sampling) with dates; chest CT and PET or whole-body staging; CA19-9 series; pre-listing operative staging report.
review.allocation: NLRB small-cirrhotic iCCA guidance requires no extrahepatic disease before the initial request and before each extension. Advanced iCCA has no standardized exception; any route would be an approved study, often with a living donor, and previous nodal or extrahepatic disease is not proposed for either.

evidence.synthesis: Published transplant programs for iCCA require liver-limited disease. ILTS–ILCA limits transplantation to cirrhotic tumours ≤3 cm without extrahepatic metastasis, or to unresectable, liver-confined disease within investigational protocols in non-cirrhotic livers; the Houston program delisted patients for extrahepatic progression. The Milan protocol explicitly excludes previously resected extrahepatic tumour spread. Programs that stage nodes surgically before listing remove node-positive patients: in Milan, 2 of 13 were node-positive at pre-listing exploration and 4 developed extrahepatic disease, while all four transplanted patients were disease-free at 8–73 months; Rennes sampled stations 8 and 12 laparoscopically before listing. Malignant regional nodes found by EUS were associated with death (HR 4.1) across cholangiocarcinoma subtypes. In the published series, early recurrences came from disease that staging missed or tolerated: the one Houston recipient with imaging-only periportal nodes (unbiopsied, PET-negative, regressed; node-negative on explant) recurred in the peritoneum at 9.7 months, which the authors attributed to perihilar-fat invasion with a positive margin; “stable” extrahepatic lesions on chemotherapy proved metastatic in 2 of 6 Houston recipients, one later explant had carcinoma in 4 of 7 hilar nodes, and in a living-donor series 2 of 6 explants with viable tumour were node-positive although the protocol included nodal biopsy at the combined laparotomy.
evidence.counterevidence: One prospective pilot admitted regional lymphadenopathy in locally advanced hilar and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: 5 of 18 reached transplantation, three were recurrence-free at 14.5–29.2 months and one had an isolated portacaval nodal recurrence at 12 months. It combined tumour types and did not require nodes to be proven malignant, so it cannot establish a cleared-node pathway, but it shows that a small subset can reach transplantation.
evidence.certainty: Low that liver-confined disease after sustained response selects better recipients; very low for transplantation after previously malignant nodes; no evidence for previously treated distant disease.
evidence.threshold_basis: Surgical sampling of stations 8 and 12 before listing follows the Milan and Rennes protocols; it is a proposed local requirement for the advanced study, not national guidance. Excluding previously resected extrahepatic spread follows Milan; NLRB requires no extrahepatic disease at the initial request and extension.

studies.design_population: 2024 ILTS–ILCA Delphi consensus with external review.
studies.selection: Cirrhotic, unresectable iCCA ≤3 cm: transplantation may be considered after a period of stability and without extrahepatic metastasis. Non-cirrhotic: only within investigational protocols for unresectable, liver-confined disease after at least six months of stability.
studies.results: No statement addresses previously treated nodal or extrahepatic disease.
studies.limits: Expert consensus.
studies.locator: Liver Transpl 2025 and Liver Cancer 2026 (PMC13271748); iCCA statements.

studies.design_population: Houston prospective neoadjuvant program for locally advanced unresectable iCCA; 32 listed, 18 transplanted.
studies.selection: Six-month gemcitabine-based induction with stability and no extrahepatic disease; extrahepatic progression prompted delisting.
studies.results: Five-year overall survival 57% from listing among recipients (49% for all 32 listed); one explant had carcinoma in 4 of 7 hilar nodes; two early recurrences arose from indeterminate pre-transplant lesions.
studies.limits: Single program; previous nodal or extrahepatic disease was not studied.
studies.locator: Am J Transplant 2022; Sections 2.1–2.2 and 3.4–3.5 (full text).

studies.design_population: Prospective intention-to-treat protocol (Milan): 13 patients with unresectable iCCA treated with chemotherapy and radioembolization.
studies.selection: Inclusion: no lymphatic or extrahepatic spread. Exclusion: prior resected extrahepatic tumour spread. Surgical sampling of stations 8 and 12 before listing; extrahepatic progression or positive nodal sampling ended the protocol.
studies.results: Nine of 13 dropped out (3 progression, 4 extrahepatic disease, 2 positive nodes at pre-listing exploration); all four transplanted patients were alive and disease-free at 8–73 months.
studies.limits: Small single-centre series.

studies.design_population: Retrospective Rennes series after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and SIRT; six transplanted.
studies.selection: Laparoscopic sampling of station 8 (common hepatic artery) and station 12 (hepatoduodenal ligament) nodes before listing; diffuse multifocal disease, macrovascular invasion and extrahepatic disease excluded.
studies.results: Five-year overall survival 100% and progression-free survival 44.4% after transplantation; three of six recurred.
studies.limits: Six recipients; retrospective.

studies.design_population: Single-centre EUS staging cohort: 157 cholangiocarcinoma patients (24 intrahepatic).
studies.selection: Consecutive EUS staging; malignant regional nodes preclude resection or transplantation at this centre.
studies.results: EUS identified regional nodes more often than cross-sectional imaging (iCCA 83% versus 50%); malignant nodes in 4 of 24 with iCCA; a malignant node was associated with death (HR 4.1).
studies.limits: Single centre; mostly perihilar disease.

studies.design_population: Prospective pilot of neoadjuvant therapy before transplantation for locally advanced hilar and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; 18 started treatment.
studies.selection: Hilar ≤3.5 cm or intrahepatic ≤8 cm; regional lymphadenopathy allowed, distant metastasis excluded.
studies.results: Eleven of 18 dropped out; five transplanted, three recurrence-free at 14.5–29.2 months, one isolated portacaval nodal recurrence at 12 months; all dropouts died (median 14.4 months from diagnosis).
studies.limits: Mixed tumour types and tiny numbers; nodal pathology not reported in the abstract.

studies.design_population: Official OPTN/NLRB guidance: Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology.
studies.selection: Small-cirrhotic iCCA: six months of stability with no new lesions or extrahepatic disease before applying; no extrahepatic disease before extending the exception.
studies.results: Allocation guidance; no outcome data.
studies.limits: Applies to the small-cirrhotic route only.

studies.design_population: Houston prospective protocol; 21 referred, 6 transplanted.
studies.selection: Excluded extrahepatic metastases and lymph-node involvement; suspicious regional nodes biopsied by EUS before treatment.
studies.results: One recipient with unbiopsied, PET-negative periportal nodes that regressed (node-negative on explant) recurred in the peritoneum at 9.7 months, attributed by the authors to perihilar-fat invasion with a positive margin; in 2 of 6, “stable” extrahepatic lesions proved metastatic after transplantation.
studies.limits: Six recipients; interim report.
studies.locator: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2018; Methods, Table 2 (full text).

studies.design_population: UPMC living-donor series, 7 recipients.
studies.selection: Unresectable, liver-confined iCCA; nodes biopsied at the combined donor–recipient laparotomy.
studies.results: 2 of 6 explants with viable tumour were node-positive although the protocol included nodal biopsy at the same laparotomy; one died at about 7 months, the other was disease-free at 2.4 years; a sub-PET-threshold lung nodule became a metastasis.
studies.limits: Seven patients.
studies.locator: Am J Transplant 2026; Results, Table 2 (full text).

studies.design_population: Single-centre series, 98 transplants for biliary cancers.
studies.selection: Explant nodal status.
studies.results: Node positivity predicted recurrence (HR 3.27, 1.32–8.10) but not overall survival (p=0.14); in the intentional pCCA/iCCA subset (n=53) the recurrence HR was 2.48 and not significant (p=0.17).
studies.limits: Mixed subtypes; nodes found on explant, not before transplantation.

edits.old: Primary site, grade, spread and disease control
edits.new: Primary site, grade and disease control

edits.old: Confirm differentiation, primary site, prior spread and the duration of disease control.
edits.new: Confirm differentiation, primary site and the duration of disease control. Previous extrahepatic disease has its own review (NET-B4).

edits.old: G3, NEC, unknown/nonportal primary and active extrahepatic disease have no active cohort in this edition. Previously resected nodes may qualify after complete clearance and the required disease-free interval; document stations and dates. Prior lung/bone/other solid-organ metastases remain outside the current opening pathway.
edits.new: G3, NEC and unknown/nonportal primary have no active cohort in this edition. Extrahepatic disease, active or previously treated, follows NET-B4: resected nodes may qualify after clearance; previous solid-organ metastases do not.

review.title: Previously treated extrahepatic disease
review.context: Use when the neuroendocrine tumor has involved sites outside the liver other than the primary (regional or distant nodes, mesentery, lung, bone or other organs), including disease later resected or treated with PRRT, ablation or radiotherapy.
review.stance: Allow previously resected nodal disease after complete clearance and ≥6 months without recurrence. Keep previous lung, bone or other solid-organ metastases closed. Nodal disease cleared only by non-surgical treatment needs individual review.
rules: Previously resected regional or mesenteric nodal disease may qualify after complete clearance, as Milan-NET requires: the primary and all extrahepatic deposits removed in a separate curative operation, no recurrence for ≥6 months after that resection, and negative SSTR PET with CT/MRI repeated within 3 months of transplant consideration. Document stations, pathology and dates.

Nodal disease that resolved only after PRRT, ablation or radiotherapy is not equivalent to resection: individual review only, with SSTR-PET-negative status for ≥6 months. Persistent SSTR-avid or morphologically visible disease is active disease.

Previous lung, bone (including a solitary treated bone lesion) or other solid-organ metastasis remains closed, including after complete treatment. The ENETS 2026 position (no macroscopic, non-targetable extrahepatic disease) is recorded as a dissent, not adopted.

Extrahepatic progression during observation or on the waiting list removes the patient from the route; re-entry needs renewed clearance and a new ≥6-month recurrence-free interval. Plan hilar lymphadenectomy at transplantation, and clear extrahepatic disease in a staged operation rather than combining major extrahepatic resection with transplantation.
review.tests: Operative and pathology reports for each extrahepatic resection, with node stations; SSTR PET (68Ga- or 64Cu-labelled) and CT/MRI within 3 months; date of the last extrahepatic treatment; PRRT cycles and response; serial imaging timeline.
review.allocation: NLRB NET guidance requires resection of the primary and extrahepatic disease with no recurrence for at least six months, a negative metastatic workup including functional imaging, de-listing on extrahepatic progression, re-consideration only after extrahepatic disease has been zeroed for at least six months, and permanent exclusion for extrahepatic solid-organ metastases such as lung or bone.

evidence.synthesis: Milan-NET requires the primary to be removed with all extrahepatic deposits in a separate curative resection before transplant consideration, with restaging six months later; in the Milan cohort, 81% of recipients had node-positive primaries and 57% had positive hilar nodes, with 10-year survival 88.8%. Previously resected regional nodal disease is therefore part of Milan-NET, not an expansion. NLRB guidance encodes the same approach, de-lists on extrahepatic progression and allows re-consideration only after extrahepatic disease has been zeroed for six months. Functional imaging changes candidacy: 68Ga-DOTATOC PET removed 7 of 15 transplant candidates because of deposits not seen on CT or MRI.
evidence.counterevidence: Nodal involvement on final pathology was associated with worse survival after transplantation in the Milan cohort (HR 5.7, univariate), and first recurrences were mostly in distant nodes and bone, so a cleared nodal history is not risk-free. Concurrent resections at transplantation (mostly of the primary or other organs) were adverse in the European registry, borderline after 2000 (HR 1.9, p=0.058), and extensive concurrent primary or multivisceral surgery was adverse in a US series; both argue for staging the primary well before transplantation. ENETS 2026 proposes replacing “no extrahepatic disease” with “no macroscopic, non-targetable extrahepatic disease” (for example isolated resectable nodes or a solitary bone lesion amenable to local treatment); the authors present this as expert opinion, not outcome-validated. In small-intestine NET, any bone metastasis was independently adverse (HR 1.94) and 21% of patients with five or fewer bone metastases progressed beyond five.
evidence.certainty: Low for accepting resected nodal disease after a recurrence-free interval; very low for PRRT-only clearance and for previous solid-organ metastases.
evidence.threshold_basis: The six-month recurrence-free interval, functional imaging, de-listing on progression and the solid-organ exclusion are NLRB wording. Repeat SSTR imaging within three months of transplant consideration follows ENETS 2026. Treating PRRT-only clearance as individual review is a conservative local choice.

studies.design_population: Milan retrospective comparison: 48 transplant and 56 resection patients with NET liver metastases.
studies.selection: Portal-drained G1/G2 primary previously resected, no extrahepatic disease, <50% liver involvement and at least six months of stable disease for transplantation.
studies.results: Node-positive primary in 19 of 24 transplanted patients with known nodal status (8 of 44 resected). Among recipients, nodal involvement on final pathology was associated with worse overall survival (HR 5.7, 95% CI 1.3–24). Recurrence after transplantation involved distant nodes in 16 of 25 and bone in 9 of 25.
studies.limits: Retrospective single centre; groups selected for different indications.
studies.locator: Am J Transplant 2022; Tables 1 and 3, univariate analysis.

studies.design_population: Milan prospective transplant versus non-transplant comparison (Milan-NET criteria).
studies.selection: Primary removed with all extrahepatic deposits in a separate curative resection before transplant consideration; restaging six months after removal; at least six months of stable disease.
studies.results: Five- and ten-year overall survival 97.2% and 88.8% with transplantation versus 50.9% and 22.4% without; 81% of recipients had node-positive primaries and 57% positive hilar nodes.
studies.limits: Benefit shown only within Milan-NET selection; previous solid-organ metastases were not included.

studies.design_population: Official OPTN/NLRB guidance: Adult MELD Exceptions for Transplant Oncology.
studies.selection: Resection of the primary and extrahepatic disease without recurrence for at least six months; negative metastatic workup including functional imaging; de-list on extrahepatic progression such as Ga-68-positive nodes; re-consider after extrahepatic disease is zeroed for at least six months; extrahepatic solid-organ metastases (lungs, bones) are a permanent exclusion.
studies.results: Allocation guidance; no outcome data.
studies.limits: Exception guidance, not an outcome-derived clinical rule.

studies.design_population: 2026 ENETS position statement on transplantation for advanced small-intestinal and pancreatic NET.
studies.selection: Replace “no EHD” with “no macroscopic, non-targetable EHD”; limited, completely resectable or otherwise controllable extrahepatic disease may not be an absolute contraindication; unresectable mesenteric nodal disease, certain bone metastases and brain metastases remain high-risk.
studies.results: No original outcome data; imaging should ideally be repeated within three months of transplant consideration.
studies.limits: Expert opinion, explicitly not outcome-validated; conflicts with the NLRB solid-organ exclusion.

studies.design_population: Single-centre imaging study: 52 NET patients comparing 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT with CT and/or MRI.
studies.selection: Fifteen were evaluated for transplantation.
studies.results: PET/CT found additional hepatic or extrahepatic metastases in 22 of 33 with liver metastases and removed 7 of 15 transplant candidates (46.6%) from further screening.
studies.limits: Small; older tracer and era.

studies.design_population: European Liver Transplant Registry: 213 transplants for NET.
studies.selection: Twenty-four had major and 60 minor additional procedures at transplantation, including extended lymphadenectomy (38), removal of the primary (29), other organ resections (such as Whipple or exenteration) and peritonectomy.
studies.results: Major concurrent resection HR 3.1 across all eras; after 2000, any concurrent resection HR 1.9 (p=0.058); five-year overall survival 52% from transplantation.
studies.limits: Historical era; heterogeneous pathology.

studies.design_population: Two Swedish centres; 138 small-intestine NET patients with bone metastases.
studies.selection: Bone metastases on SSTR-PET; rarely biopsied; never curatively treated.
studies.results: Any bone metastasis HR 1.94; more than five lesions: median survival 18 vs 75 months; 21% with five or fewer progressed beyond five.
studies.limits: Small-intestine NET only.

studies.design_population: Multicentre cohort, 28 centres (mostly US, also Canadian and European); 85 transplants for NET.
studies.selection: “Extent of resection” meant concurrent primary or multivisceral surgery at transplantation, not clearance of metastases.
studies.results: Extensive concurrent surgery associated with worse survival (p=0.015).
studies.limits: No extrahepatic-disease variable; historical era.
studies.locator: J Surg Oncol 2015; Methods and Results (full text).

edits.old: as three separate closed transplant strata.
edits.new: as three separate closed transplant strata. Distant or peritoneal metastasis, even after response, ends the transplant route.

edits.old: These proposed expansions remain closed.
edits.new: These proposed expansions remain closed. Distant or peritoneal disease at any time ends the route.

edits.rule: Distant or peritoneal metastasis, or nodal disease beyond the regional field, found at any time (including at operative staging) ends the transplant route for this protocol, even after response to chemoradiation or chemotherapy. There is no proposed stratum.

edits.old: These are not equivalent exposures.
edits.new: These are not equivalent exposures. Record any distant or peritoneal finding at staging with its pathology.

edits.old: Imaging-negative nodes do not equal pathological clearance.
edits.new: Imaging-negative nodes do not equal pathological clearance. Operative staging is where most of this disease is found: in the Mayo series, 36 of 199 patients left the protocol with metastases found at staging (regional nodes 14, intrahepatic 6, extrahepatic 16).

edits.old: Soliman's occult-node recipients do not validate deliberate nodal expansion.
edits.new: Soliman's occult-node recipients do not validate deliberate nodal expansion. One prospective pilot admitted regional lymphadenopathy in locally advanced hilar and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; five of 18 reached transplantation and one had an isolated portacaval nodal recurrence at 12 months. Whether the nodes were proven malignant is not reported in the abstract, and it cannot validate a cleared-node stratum.

edits.old: Local recipients had 26 recurrences;
edits.new: Of 62 dropouts, 36 had metastases found at operative staging (regional nodes 14, intrahepatic 6, extrahepatic 16). Local recipients had 26 recurrences;

study.design_population: Prospective pilot of neoadjuvant therapy before transplantation for locally advanced hilar and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; 18 started treatment.
study.selection: Hilar ≤3.5 cm or intrahepatic ≤8 cm; regional lymphadenopathy allowed, distant metastasis excluded.
study.results: Eleven of 18 dropped out; five transplanted, three recurrence-free at 14.5–29.2 months, one isolated portacaval nodal recurrence at 12 months.
study.limits: Mixed tumour types and tiny numbers; nodal pathology not reported in the abstract.

edits.old: Start with liver-only disease and no macrovascular invasion; do not automatically broaden access using stable extrahepatic disease or an explant score.
edits.new: Start with liver-only disease and no macrovascular invasion. Define a separate extrahepatic stratum, not yet activated: lung-only disease that is stable for ≥6 months or completely resected or ablated. Bone, serosal and progressive extrahepatic disease stay closed. Do not select using an explant score.

edits.old: Extrahepatic disease is a separate unactivated stratum requiring case-specific discussion, not a national absolute prohibition.
edits.new: Extrahepatic disease is not a national absolute prohibition, but it is outside the opening cohort.

edits.old: Record the guideline disagreement explicitly. A future EHD proposal must specify site, control duration, symptoms, comparator and independent review; “stable EHD” alone is insufficient.
edits.new: Proposed extrahepatic stratum (defined, not activated): lung-only disease without pleural involvement, asymptomatic, and either stable on serial imaging for ≥6 months or completely resected or ablated with no recurrence for ≥6 months. Each case needs independent expert review and a written comparison with observation or systemic treatment.

edits.rule: Closed: bone metastasis; pleural, peritoneal or other serosal disease; extrahepatic disease outside the lung; and progressive or symptomatic extrahepatic disease. Record the guideline disagreement in every case. Hilar nodal involvement is a recurrence risk factor rather than an extrahepatic exclusion; plan hilar lymphadenectomy.

edits.old: technical resectability and alternative-treatment review.
edits.new: technical resectability and alternative-treatment review. Record each extrahepatic site, its size and serial imaging dates, and any resection or ablation record.

edits.old: Histology-derived risk scoring cannot be substituted for preoperative staging.
edits.new: Histology-derived risk scoring cannot be substituted for preoperative staging. In the first European registry report, 10 of 59 recipients had extrahepatic disease before or at transplantation, with 1-, 5- and 10-year survival of 90%, 80% and 80% versus 94%, 83% and 70% without it. In a Mayo cohort of 80 patients, bone metastasis was independently associated with mortality (HR 6.3) whereas lung metastasis was not (HR 0.8).

edits.old: does not establish benefit over observation or systemic options for all sites/burdens.
edits.new: does not establish benefit over observation or systemic options for all sites/burdens. The 2021 consensus advises that transplantation should not be proposed with extrahepatic disease (level V, grade A). Registry subgroups are small, extrahepatic sites and their treatment are poorly described, and the Mayo site analysis covers all treatments, not transplant recipients alone.

edits.old: very low for causal EHD benefit or pre-LT score-driven selection.
edits.new: very low for causal EHD benefit, for the proposed lung-only stratum, or for pre-LT score-driven selection.

edits.item: Lung-only stratum with ≥6 months of stability or completed treatment: lung metastasis was not adverse in the Mayo site analysis whereas bone was; six months follows the DGVS stable-disease recommendation and the registry finding that a short wait (≤120 days) predicted recurrence. Excluding pleural and other serosal disease is a conservative local choice not tested in transplant series.

study.design_population: European Liver Transplant Registry: 59 recipients transplanted for HEHE.
study.selection: Ten (16.9%) had extrahepatic disease before or at transplantation; three had extrahepatic surgery before transplantation.
study.results: One-, five- and ten-year survival 90%, 80% and 80% with extrahepatic disease versus 94%, 83% and 70% without; lymph-node invasion also did not significantly change survival, whereas vascular invasion did.
study.limits: Ten patients with extrahepatic disease; sites and treatment not separated.

study.design_population: Mayo cohort of 80 patients with HEHE (24 transplanted, 26 resected, 30 managed medically).
study.selection: Twenty-six had extrahepatic metastases at diagnosis, four of them in the transplant group.
study.results: Bone metastasis was independently associated with long-term mortality (HR 6.3); lung metastasis was not (HR 0.8).
study.limits: The site analysis covers all treatments; only four recipients had extrahepatic disease.

edits.old: The combined outside-criteria group had recurrence hazard ratio 2.98.
edits.new: The combined outside-criteria group had recurrence hazard ratio 2.98. Staging found metastases in 17%; four patients were transplanted with metastatic disease, pooled with the outside-criteria group; one centre accepted N0–N1 nodes within the hepatoduodenal ligament. No separate outcome exists for nodal disease.

study.design_population: Mayo protocol; 215 started neoadjuvant treatment, 63 fell out.
study.selection: EUS-FNA of regional nodes before chemoradiation since 2003; operative staging with hepatic-artery and pericholedochal node biopsy.
study.results: At staging: positive nodes 19, peritoneal metastases 14, local extension 11 (overlapping); median survival after the staging operation 6.0 months; EUS-FNA before chemoradiation lowered the positive-staging rate to 15%.
study.locator: Am J Clin Oncol 2016; Results (full text).

study.design_population: AHPBA 2015 expert consensus on hilar cholangiocarcinoma.
study.selection: Suspicious regional nodes: EUS or laparoscopic FNA; transplant excluded with metastases; operative biopsy of hepatic artery and pericholedochal nodes.
study.locator: HPB 2015; transplant and staging sections (full text).

study.design_population: Single-centre series, 98 transplants for biliary cancers.
study.results: Node positivity predicted recurrence (HR 3.27) but not overall survival (p=0.14); not significant in the intentional pCCA/iCCA subset (HR 2.48, p=0.17).
study.limits: Mixed subtypes; nodes found on explant.

edits.old: Matched 5-year DFS: EHD 73.5% versus 81.6% without, P=.54.
edits.new: Pre-transplant extrahepatic disease was mostly radiological lung disease (23 of 40), and only 5 had lung surgery beforehand; extrahepatic disease HR 1.5 (0.8–3.0), not retained. Matched 5-year DFS: EHD 73.5% versus 81.6% without, P=.54.

study.design_population: MSKCC clinicopathological cohort, 93 EHE at all sites.
study.selection: Nodal and pleural involvement recorded; one liver transplant.
study.results: Nodal involvement HR 2.7; five-year survival 30% with nodal and 22% with pleural disease versus over 70% without (unadjusted).
